source_research.title: Microsoft GROUPBY function
source_research.claim: GROUPBY groups and aggregates along one axis; supported in Excel for Microsoft 365.

source_research.title: Microsoft PIVOTBY function
source_research.claim: PIVOTBY groups across two axes; it is not the same feature as PivotTable.

source_research.title: Microsoft TRIMRANGE function
source_research.claim: TRIMRANGE removes blank outer rows and columns, not internal blank rows.

episodes.working_title: One Excel Formula Turns 8 Sales Rows Into 3 Totals

narration.text: Eight sales rows. Three products. One formula. Watch the totals appear.
The source table has product names in column A and revenue in column C.
In Microsoft 365 Excel, enter GROUPBY with the products, revenue, and SUM.
A totals three hundred, B three hundred, C one hundred twenty. That's seven hundred twenty.
Reconcile the result to the source sum before you trust it.

episodes.proof: Show actual Excel formula and 3 result rows; separately show =SUM(C2:C9) equals 720.
episodes.visual_plan: 9:16 real Excel screen recording or transparently labeled accurate UI reconstruction; macro crop formula bar and totals; no slide deck
episodes.caveat: Availability depends on Microsoft 365 Excel; no claim tested in Excel until capture verified
qa: Actual formula behavior in supported Excel
Clean audio captions and no false UI

episodes.working_title: Excel GROUPBY vs PIVOTBY vs PivotTable: Same Data, Different Jobs
episodes.hook: Three ways to summarize the same sales. One works on one axis, another on two, and a third uses an interactive PivotTable.

chapters.title: The challenge
chapters.narration: Eight fictional sales rows totaling seven hundred twenty. We need totals by product and by quarter. Can one method handle both cleanly?
chapters.shot: Live dataset in Excel with sum proof; clearly marked synthetic.

chapters.title: GROUPBY
chapters.narration: GROUPBY is a one-axis formula summary. Enter the product field, revenue values and SUM; check three product totals. The one-axis layout is the key limitation.

chapters.title: PIVOTBY
chapters.narration: PIVOTBY adds a column grouping dimension. Use product and quarter as axes, with revenue as values. The quarter totals should be four hundred fifty and two hundred seventy.
chapters.shot: Show =PIVOTBY(A2:A9,B2:B9,C2:C9,SUM); verify A 200/100, B 200/100, C 50/70 and grand total 720.

chapters.title: PivotTable
chapters.narration: A PivotTable is an interactive feature, not the PIVOTBY formula. Add Product to Rows, Quarter to Columns, Revenue to Values; compare totals and discuss refresh behavior.
chapters.shot: Record actual Insert > PivotTable UI, inspect SUM not COUNT, demonstrate refresh of a changed source row without implying automatic refresh.

chapters.title: What breaks
chapters.narration: Older Excel versions may not have these newer functions. A changed source range or wrong value aggregation can produce misleading totals. Check your version, range and grand total.
chapters.shot: Show genuine compatibility check and one controlled error or range extension; never fabricate Excel outputs.

chapters.title: Decision
chapters.narration: Use GROUPBY for a quick one-axis formula, PIVOTBY for two-axis formulas, and PivotTable for interactive analysis. The best tool is the one whose output you can verify.
chapters.shot: Comparison grounded in the live demo, with concise end card.

thumbnail.visual: Split Excel formula summaries with contrasting 1-axis and 2-axis results; no invented endorsement

qa: Actual PivotTable recorded or clearly marked reconstructed
episodes.caveat: No measured speed comparison; compatibility to be checked in target Excel version.

episodes.working_title: TRIMRANGE Removes the Blank Edges—Not the Blank Middle

narration.text: Your Excel range includes blank rows. But watch which blanks this formula actually removes.
This example has data from B3 through D7, surrounded by empty rows and columns.
TRIMRANGE on A1 to E12 cuts off the empty outer edges.
The blank row inside the data stays. It is not a delete-empty-rows command.
Trim the edges, then verify the resulting range.

episodes.proof: Synthetic A1:E12 with nonempty B3:D4 and B6:D7, empty B5:D5; expected trimmed range is B3:D7 with interior blank row retained.
episodes.visual_plan: 9:16 accurate Excel demonstration; colored boundary overlay before/after; no false claim that workbook file size or UsedRange is repaired
episodes.caveat: Microsoft 365 availability; TRIMRANGE trims edges of the referenced range, not interior blanks or physical worksheet rows.
